trackers.monetization_model: Kochava sells measurement and attribution to app developers, and runs a data marketplace, the Kochava Collective, through its subsidiary Collective Data Solutions. Under a 2025 class settlement, data the SDK collects may be used only for the app that collected it (Kochava's 2022 open letter; court order of 2025-11-14).

consequences.text: In 2026 a US federal court entered an order, agreed with the US FTC, that for 10 years bars Kochava and its data marketplace subsidiary from selling or sharing location data tied to sensitive places in the US, such as medical facilities, places of worship and shelters. The FTC had charged that Kochava sold such data; Kochava neither admitted nor denied it.
consequences.wording: Settled with the US FTC: a court order entered 2026-06-25. Kochava neither admitted nor denied the charges.

procedural_note.text: The FTC sued in 2022 and also charged that Kochava's free SDK sent it what people did in apps, which it sold. The court dismissed the first complaint with leave to amend in 2023 and refused to dismiss the amended complaints in 2024 and 2025.

consequences.text: In 2025 a US federal court approved Kochava's settlement of a class action brought for people who said Kochava sold their data, including location, without consent. Kochava must keep data its SDK collects for the app that collected it, delete older SDK data it kept for itself, and filter out location data tied to sensitive places. Kochava denied the claims.
consequences.wording: A class action settled with a court's approval on 2025-11-14; Kochava denied the claims.

consequences.text: Kochava said in 2019 that data from apps on its free plan, Free App Analytics, was the backbone of its data marketplace, the Kochava Collective, while paying clients' data was kept apart; in 2020 it told free-plan apps to say they may sell identifiers and geolocation data to third parties. FinePrint can't see which plan an app uses.
consequences.wording: According to Kochava's 2019 press release and 2020 notice to Free App Analytics customers; a 2025 settlement now limits SDK data to the app that collected it.
